' || split_part(b.nom, ' ', 2)) IN (SELECT kyc_nom FROM kyc) AND b.nom IN (SELECT nom_complet FROM effaceurs);
hints: Dans une CTE récursive PostgreSQL, chaque colonne doit avoir exactement le même type dans les deux parties : caste la part de départ en float8 (pct est en double precision) et l'horodatage de départ en TIMESTAMP.

22.S.solution: WITH RECURSIVE chaine(siren, part) AS (SELECT importateur_siren, 100.0::float8 FROM conteneurs WHERE code = 'MSCU-449120' UNION ALL SELECT p.detenteur, c.part * p.pct / 100 FROM participations p JOIN chaine c ON p.detenue = c.siren), b AS (SELECT REPLACE(siren, 'PERSONNE:', '') AS nom, part FROM chaine WHERE siren LIKE 'PERSONNE:%') SELECT b.nom AS beneficiaire, ROUND(b.part::numeric, 1) AS part, w.plateforme, w.adresse, (SELECT ROUND(SUM(montant)::numeric, 2) FROM tx_crypto WHERE vers = w.adresse) AS recu FROM b JOIN wallets w ON w.kyc_nom = UPPER(left(b.nom, 1) || '. string_agg(DISTINCT host, ',' ORDER BY host) AS liste ... GROUP BY process HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT host) <= 2 ORDER BY process.

34.2.solution: SELECT horodatage, host, process, ligne_commande FROM process_logs WHERE ligne_commande ~* '(-enc|hidden|/create|lsass)' ORDER BY horodatage;
hints: L'opérateur ~* teste une expression régulière sans tenir compte de la casse : une seule alternative (a|b|c) remplace quatre LIKE.
WHERE ligne_commande ~* '(-enc|hidden|/create|lsass)' ORDER BY horodatage (ou quatre LOWER(...) LIKE '%...%').
34.2.note: ~* est l'expression régulière insensible à la casse de PostgreSQL ; LOWER(...) LIKE fonctionne aussi.

FROM process_logs f JOIN process_logs p ON p.host = f.host AND p.pid = f.ppid WHERE f.host = 'PC-COMPTA-07' AND f.horodatage BETWEEN ... ORDER BY f.horodatage.

34.5.solution: WITH r AS (SELECT * FROM process_logs WHERE process = 'rundll32.exe' AND ligne_commande LIKE '%upd.dll%'), g AS (SELECT host, MIN(horodatage) AS premiere, COUNT(*) AS executions FROM r GROUP BY host) SELECT g.host, g.premiere, g.executions, p.process AS parent_premiere FROM g JOIN r ON r.host = g.host AND r.horodatage = g.premiere LEFT JOIN process_logs p ON p.host = r.host AND p.pid = r.ppid ORDER BY g.premiere;

JOIN postes p ON p.ip = a.source_ip AND p.type = 'poste' WHERE a.resultat = 'succes' AND p.utilisateur <> a.login ORDER BY a.horodatage.

35.4.solution: SELECT a.login, d.lieu, COUNT(*) AS connexions, MIN(a.horodatage) AS premiere, MAX(a.horodatage) AS derniere FROM auth_logs a JOIN deplacements d ON d.login = a.login AND a.horodatage BETWEEN d.debut AND d.fin WHERE a.resultat = 'succes' AND a.methode <> 'vpn' GROUP BY a.login, d.lieu;

35.5.solution: WITH RECURSIVE aretes AS (SELECT p.hostname AS src, a.dest_host AS dest, a.horodatage AS t FROM auth_logs a JOIN postes p ON p.ip = a.source_ip WHERE a.login = 'adm.varenne' AND a.resultat = 'succes' AND a.horodatage >= '2028-03-06'), c(dest, chemin, t) AS (SELECT dest, src || ' > ' || dest, t FROM aretes WHERE src = 'PC-COMPTA-07' UNION ALL SELECT e.dest, c.chemin || ' > ' || e.dest, e.t FROM c JOIN aretes e ON e.src = c.dest AND e.t > c.t AND strpos(c.chemin, e.dest) = 0) SELECT chemin, t AS arrivee FROM c WHERE dest = 'DC01';
hints: Construis d'abord les arêtes (machine source, machine destination, horodatage) ; une CTE récursive avance de saut en saut, toujours plus tard dans le temps.
c(dest, chemin, t) : départ depuis 'PC-COMPTA-07', puis JOIN aretes e ON e.src = c.dest AND e.t > c.t AND strpos(c.chemin, e.dest) = 0 (pas de boucle) ; garde dest = 'DC01'.

35.A.solution: SELECT a.login, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXTRACT(HOUR FROM a.horodatage) < 6) AS nuit, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXTRACT(HOUR FROM a.horodatage) BETWEEN 6 AND 19) AS jour, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXTRACT(HOUR FROM a.horodatage) >= 20) AS soir FROM auth_logs a JOIN comptes_ad c ON c.login = a.login WHERE c.admin = 1 AND a.resultat = 'succes' GROUP BY a.login ORDER BY a.login;

COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXTRACT(HOUR FROM a.horodatage) < 6) AS nuit, ... BETWEEN 6 AND 19 ... AS jour, ... >= 20 ... AS soir, GROUP BY a.login ORDER BY a.login.

35.S.solution: WITH RECURSIVE aretes AS (SELECT p.hostname AS src, a.dest_host AS dest, a.horodatage AS t FROM auth_logs a JOIN postes p ON p.ip = a.source_ip WHERE a.login = 'adm.varenne' AND a.resultat = 'succes' AND a.horodatage >= '2028-03-06'), c(dest, chemin, t, depart) AS (SELECT dest, src || ' > ' || dest, t, t FROM aretes WHERE src = 'PC-COMPTA-07' UNION ALL SELECT e.dest, c.chemin || ' > ' || e.dest, e.t, c.depart FROM c JOIN aretes e ON e.src = c.dest AND e.t > c.t AND strpos(c.chemin, e.dest) = 0) SELECT DISTINCT c.chemin, c.depart, c.t AS arrivee FROM c JOIN postes po ON po.hostname = c.dest WHERE po.type = 'ot';

36.2.solution: SELECT horodatage, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM horodatage - LAG(horodatage) OVER (ORDER BY horodatage))) AS ecart_s FROM proxy_logs WHERE host = 'PC-COMPTA-07' AND domaine = 'cdn-update-check.net' ORDER BY horodatage LIMIT 10;
hints: horodatage - LAG(horodatage) OVER (ORDER BY horodatage) est un interval ; EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ...) le convertit en secondes.

36.3.solution: WITH iv AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, horodatage, octets_out, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM horodatage - LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage)) AS dt FROM proxy_logs), st AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, COUNT(dt) AS n, AVG(dt) AS m, stddev_pop(dt) AS sd FROM iv WHERE dt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY host, domaine, ip_dest HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50) SELECT host, domaine, n AS intervalles, ROUND(m) AS moyenne_s, ROUND(sd, 1) AS ecart_type, ROUND(sd / m, 3) AS cv FROM st ORDER BY cv, host;

CTE iv avec dt = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM horodatage - LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage)), CTE st avec COUNT(dt), AVG(dt), stddev_pop(dt) ... HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50, puis ROUND(sd / m, 3) AS cv.

36.4.solution: WITH iv AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, horodatage, octets_out, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM horodatage - LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage)) AS dt FROM proxy_logs), st AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, COUNT(dt) AS n, AVG(dt) AS m, stddev_pop(dt) AS sd FROM iv WHERE dt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY host, domaine, ip_dest HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50) SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, ROUND(m) AS moyenne_s FROM st WHERE sd / m < 0.05 AND domaine NOT IN (SELECT domaine FROM domaines_connus);

36.S.solution: WITH iv AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, horodatage, octets_out, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM horodatage - LAG(horodatage) OVER (PARTITION BY host, domaine ORDER BY horodatage)) AS dt FROM proxy_logs), st AS (SELECT host, domaine, ip_dest, COUNT(dt) AS n, AVG(dt) AS m, stddev_pop(dt) AS sd FROM iv WHERE dt IS NOT NULL GROUP BY host, domaine, ip_dest HAVING COUNT(dt) >= 50), b AS (SELECT DISTINCT host, domaine FROM st WHERE sd / m < 0.05 AND domaine NOT IN (SELECT domaine FROM domaines_connus)), t AS (SELECT b.host, (SELECT MIN(horodatage) FROM process_logs p WHERE p.host = b.host AND p.process = 'rundll32.exe' AND p.ligne_commande LIKE '%upd.dll%') AS chargement, (SELECT MIN(horodatage) FROM proxy_logs x WHERE x.host = b.host AND x.domaine = b.domaine) AS premier_battement, (SELECT MAX(horodatage) FROM proxy_logs x WHERE x.host = b.host AND x.domaine = b.domaine) AS dernier_battement FROM b) SELECT host, chargement, premier_battement, dernier_battement, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM premier_battement - chargement)) AS secondes FROM t ORDER BY chargement;

38.1.solution: WITH m AS (SELECT horodatage, valeur, AVG(valeur) OVER (ORDER BY horodatage ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS moyenne FROM capteurs WHERE site = 'Réservoir Montsouris') SELECT horodatage, valeur, ROUND(moyenne::numeric, 2) AS moyenne, ROUND((100.0 * (valeur - moyenne) / moyenne)::numeric) AS ecart_pct FROM m WHERE horodatage::date = '2028-03-12' AND ABS(valeur - moyenne) / moyenne > 0.2 ORDER BY horodatage;
hints: valeur est en double precision : la moyenne aussi, et ROUND(x, 2) exige un numeric en PostgreSQL, caste avec ::numeric.
CTE m avec AVG(valeur) OVER (ORDER BY horodatage ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), puis WHERE horodatage::date = '2028-03-12' AND ABS(valeur - moyenne) / moyenne > 0.2.
